name: struct-aos
axis: array-of-structs traversal — read 2 of 4 i32 fields from every record; the A side of the AoS/SoA layout A/B
n: N=1000000 records of 4 i32, ROUNDS=500 (500M record reads)
nPython: N=1000000, ROUNDS=60 (8.33x fewer rounds; multiply Python's wall time by 8.33 to compare)
notes:
Byte-identical output to struct-soa, so the two directories are a clean layout A/B — divide one wall time by the other. Rust holds a Vec

(32MB contiguous); VL holds a WasmGC array of struct references and JS an Array of objects, so both pointer-chase one indirection per element. Python uses a class with __slots__. The `^ r` in the reduction makes each round's sum genuinely round-dependent so no round is loop-invariant. Construction of the 1M records is ~7% of the VL wall time at ROUNDS=500. Scale-verified by doubling ROUNDS at the shipped ROUNDS=500: vl 1.92x, rs 1.73x, js 1.80x, py 1.94x (the sub-2x ratios are the fixed record-construction cost, which does not scale with ROUNDS).

audit.rustVectorised: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT — rustc -O AUTO-VECTORISES this loop and no meta note said so. Confirmed by disassembling `main::main`: the hot loop is SSE2 packed integer arithmetic (12 packed ops). rustc's default target is baseline x86-64, so this is 128-bit SSE2; `rustc -O -C target-cpu=native` widens it further. The Rust:VL multiple on this benchmark is therefore mostly SIMD WIDTH, not scalar codegen quality — VL emits no SIMD. Report it as such.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
